A Roth IRA is a tax-advantaged retirement account. You contribute after-tax dollars now, your investments grow tax-free, and you can withdraw both contributions and earnings tax-free in retirement (usually after age 59½ and the account has been open at least 5 years). There are income limits and annual contribution limits, and you can’t deduct Roth contributions on your current tax return.

Key points:
- Contributions are not tax-deductible upfront, but qualified withdrawals are tax-free.
- Earnings grow tax-free; you don’t pay capital gains tax on withdrawals.
- 2026 contribution limit is $7,500 if you’re under 50, or $8,600 if you’re 50 or older (catch-up). Note: actual limits can vary by year; check the latest IRS rules.
- Income limits apply for eligibility to contribute directly (phased out at higher incomes; there are backdoor Roth options if you’re high income).
- You can contribute to a Roth IRA even if you have a 401(k) at work, subject to those limits.
- You must take required minimum distributions (RMDs) never? Roth IRAs have no RMDs for the original owner, which is aPlus.

If you want, tell me your filing status and approximate income, and I’ll outline whether you’re likely eligible to contribute directly and what your rough annual limit would be. Also I can compare Roth vs Traditional IRA so you can see which fits you better. 

Sources:
- https://www.irs.gov
- general Roth IRA principles (IRS and investor education sites)

That notification looks like a bank alert scam prompt. Do not click any links or enter credentials. Here’s how to tell:

- The message asks you to verify identity via a vague link. Legit banks rarely request sensitive verification via a direct link in a text.
- It asks you to opt out or respond. Scammers use urgency to get you to reveal info or install malware.
- You mentioned a connected broker link earlier. If you didn’t initiate a sign-in, ignore it.

What to do now:
- Do not reply, tap, or enter any info.
- If you’re worried, log directly into your bank app from your saved bookmark (not from the text link) and check for any alerts there.
- If you suspect a real issue, contact your bank’s official customer service number from their site to confirm.

Want me to check whether you’ve got any active alerts in your bank app or on your broker account? I can guide you step by step.
